question: When was the Bengal Partition Plan implemented?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mon Oct 16 1905**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bengal Partition Plan was announced in December 1903 by Lord Curzon, the then Viceroy of India.
 
• The official implementation of the Bengal Partition Plan took place on **16 October 1905**.
 
• The partition separated the largely Muslim eastern areas from the largely Hindu western areas.
 
• The main reason for the partition was to improve administrative efficiency in the large and populous Bengal province.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Curzon**

 
 
• George Nathaniel Curzon, 1st Marquess Curzon of Kedleston, served as Viceroy of India from 1899 to 1905.
 
• His tenure is noted for major administrative reforms and a policy of divide and rule.
 
• Curzon’s policies aimed at strengthening British control over India but faced strong opposition from Indian nationalists.
 
 
 
• **Swadeshi Movement**
 
 
• In response to the partition, the Indian National Congress launched the Swadeshi Movement, promoting the use of Indian-made goods and boycotting British products.
 
• The movement marked the beginning of a new phase of the Indian independence struggle, emphasizing self-reliance and indigenous enterprise.
 
• It led to the establishment of Indian industries, schools, and national institutions.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Partition**
 
 
• The partition created communal tensions between Hindus and Muslims, leading to widespread protests and unrest.
 
• It eventually forced the British government to revoke the partition in 1911, reuniting Bengal.
 
• The episode intensified the Indian nationalist movement and sowed the seeds for future communal divisions.
